chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ma'alla Abu Uthman, from Ma'la ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who buys goods and then rents them out. He said, 'There is no harm in it.' And he ordered me, so I spoke to a man regarding that matter.

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia jurisprudence to buy goods and then rent them out?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* validates the permissibility of *istiwda'* (renting out goods), a common commercial practice in early Shia jurisprudence. The Imam’s directive for the narrator to consult another individual highlights the scholarly tradition of verifying specific market rulings through expert testimony, ensuring the transaction aligns with Islamic commercial ethics.
